assumptions: Daniel is Player One and Nik is Player Two; both enter their real signings fairly.
Chromium runs the unchanged local game screens. A prepared, already-started Showdown uses the real transfer rules in Node and retains locked moves between page loads.

Unfinished signing entry is treated as progress worth recovering. The Rule Book does not explicitly promise unfinished-entry recovery, so this finding is likely. There is no loss of already-locked signings or saved verdicts.
title: Reloading halfway through signing entry clears unfinished signings
steps: Start season 1 of a 3-season Showdown; both friends lock their guesses.
Daniel enters Paulo Dybala, Italy Serie A, Argentina, but does not lock his signings.
Wait one second. A normal challenge refresh keeps the row.
Reload the page, reopen the same season, and continue the replay to signing entry.
expected: Daniel's unfinished signing returns so he can finish entering his three signings.
actual: Player name, previous league and nationality all return blank. Both friends' locked guesses remain. The same loss occurred at season 10 of 10. Locked signings and completed verdicts survive reload.
root_cause: The shared signing screen keeps unfinished rows only in the page. Reopening after a page load clears both forms and restores locked inputs only. The older draft-save handlers check for a local recording challenge, which this shared screen does not create.

fix.change: Remember each friend's unfinished signing rows for this Showdown and season, restore them after reload, and clear them only after a successful lock. Keep locked signings and completed verdicts as the final record.
